answer.justification: Only logit measurements are available. The logit shift is large: KL 0.432, top-1 agreement 0.828, TV 0.173 and Token-DiFR gap 0.845. That magnitude fits only the system-prompt classes (KL above about 0.2). The weight-based classes sit far lower: fine-tune backdoor has KL 0.15 and top-1 0.909, and fine-tune bias and quantization are lower still. Between the two system-prompt classes, every magnitude measure is beyond even the backdoor's values (KL 0.30, TV 0.139, top-1 0.866, DiFR 0.47). The document calls the backdoor the class furthest from the reference, so that ordering favours it. The raw-score shift ÷ TV of 3.1 points the other way: it is nearer the bias value (3.4) than the backdoor value (3.9). It is also near fine-tune backdoor (3.3), but that class's other logit values are far off. Without text, which is what normally separates the bias from the backdoor, the choice between them is close to a coin flip, tilted toward backdoor by the overall magnitude.
